title: Search Projection
description: Schema for the OpenSearch search-projection document. This is the read-model contract between the projection builder and the BFF. It includes canonical fields copied forward, derived metrics, and denormalized joins. Runtime fields (e.g., search highlight snippets) are NOT part of this schema — they are attached at query time.

record_kind.description: Discriminator selecting which logical record this projection row carries. Drives client-side rendering and join policy.

document_id.description: Canonical document ID. Copied from canonical output.

title.description: Document title. Copied from canonical output.

jurisdiction.description: Back-compat ISO 3166 jurisdiction code copied from canonical output. New consumers should prefer `jurisdiction_ids` for canonical filtering. MUST match contracts/vocabularies/jurisdiction.json.

jurisdiction_ids.description: Canonical jurisdiction IDs this row belongs to. Drives the canonical `jur_*` search filters; ISO `jurisdiction` remains for back-compat and is ANDed with this when both are present.

authority_ids.description: Canonical authority IDs attached to this row. Optional for `legal_document` rows (primary statutes are commonly attributed by jurisdiction alone); required for `commentary_insight` rows via the conditional below.

source_document_ids.description: Canonical primary documents referenced by this row. Empty for `legal_document` rows; required and non-empty for `commentary_insight` rows so the UI can resolve back to source.

document_type.description: Normalized document type. Copied from canonical output. MUST match contracts/vocabularies/document-type.json.

authority_name.description: Human-readable court or issuing-authority label denormalized for UI composition.

official_citation.description: Canonical official publication citation denormalized for UI trust metadata.

original_language.description: Original source language used for translation-state labeling.

translation_status.description: Translation state of the content exposed to the UI.

is_official.description: Whether the source origin is official and can be surfaced as a trust signal.

language.description: Primary language (ISO 639-1). Copied from canonical output.

effective_date.description: Effective date. Copied from canonical output.

lifecycle_status.description: Lifecycle state copied from the document.processed event payload.

level.description: Derived: rank of this norm in the hierarchy of norms (ADR-0033), sourced from the row's jurisdiction — never guessed from its text. When a row carries several jurisdictions the most specific one wins. Absent when the jurisdiction is unknown to contracts/vocabularies/jurisdiction-hierarchy.json (the row is then unreachable through `norm_hierarchy()`, which the endpoint reports as a coverage gap rather than papering over) and absent for `commentary_insight` rows, which are not norms and govern nothing.

subordinate_to.description: Derived: the jurisdictions whose law outranks this norm, most authoritative first — a Zurich communal ordinance is subordinate to `jur_ch_zh` and to `jur_ch_federal`. This is what makes preemption answerable by traversal instead of similarity. Note the edge points at SCOPES, not documents: subordination in law is scope-wide (the ordinance is subordinate to the whole body of cantonal and federal law, not to one act), so a document→document edge would be a fiction. Each scope's own level is recoverable from the jurisdiction-hierarchy vocabulary.

delegates_to.description: Competence this norm delegates downward — the cantonal clause that lets a commune legislate at all, and therefore the difference between an ordinance that is authorised and one that is ultra vires. UNPOPULATED TODAY: unlike `subordinate_to` it is not derivable from the jurisdiction tree, because it is an assertion made by the norm's text. Shape mirrors `delegates_to` in document.schema.json so the extracted edge can be projected without a schema change.

in_force_from.description: First date the norm was in force. Coalesced from the canonical document's `in_force_from`, falling back to `effective_date`, so the index carries ONE field to range-query when answering `check_in_force(id, date)`.

in_force_until.description: Last date the norm WAS in force — inclusive. Absent means 'not known to be repealed', which is not the same as 'never repealed': a row with `lifecycle_status: repealed` and no date here resolves to `unknown`, never to a guessed boolean.

structural_path.description: Intrinsic document hierarchy path. Copied from canonical output.

content.description: Full text content for search indexing and snippet generation.

content_docling.description: DoclingDocument JSON (ADR-0010). Stored for detail view pass-through. May be large — consider indexing constraints.

sections_count.description: Derived: count of sections belonging to this document. Computed by the projection builder from the sections index.

citations_count.description: Derived: count of citations from this document. Computed by the projection builder from the citations index.

related_decisions_count.description: Derived: count of related decision documents. Computed by reverse citation join.

related_commentary_count.description: Derived: count of related commentary documents. Computed by reverse citation join.

content_preview.description: Derived: first ~200 characters of content for lightweight display without loading the full document.

source_id.description: Lineage: source ID. Copied from canonical output.

processed_at.description: Timestamp when the canonical document was processed.
